seoTitle: How to Connect Gmail to ChatGPT for Inbox Automation
metaDescription: Two ways to bring ChatGPT into Gmail: OpenAI's own chat-side connector, and a browser extension that puts drafting tools directly in the compose window.
intro: OpenAI now ships its own Gmail connector inside ChatGPT, on paid plans, so it's no longer accurate to say ChatGPT can't reach Gmail at all. That connector works from the ChatGPT side: you open a chat and ask it to search, summarize, or draft from your inbox. It doesn't put anything inside the Gmail compose window itself. If you want suggestions appearing right where you type, a browser extension is still the route, and that's the setup this guide walks through: installing one, using it inside a real compose window, and where the placeholder text it leaves behind trips people up.
costNote: Browser extensions for this typically have a free tier with limited generations and a paid tier for unlimited use, priced by the extension's own developer. OpenAI's chat-side Gmail connector, the alternative described above, needs a paid ChatGPT plan; it isn't included on the free tier.

steps.heading: Find and vet an extension in the Chrome Web Store
steps.body: Search the Chrome Web Store for an extension that adds ChatGPT drafting tools to Gmail's compose window. Because an extension like this needs permission to read and modify everything on the Gmail page, check the developer, rating, and install count before adding anything to an inbox you rely on. A Google Workspace Marketplace listing is worth weighing too, since those go through Google's own review process; the ChatGPT-for-Gmail add-on currently there, for example, lists its publisher and shows real install and review numbers you can check before granting access.

image.caption: The Chrome Web Store listing for a ChatGPT-Gmail extension, showing its rating, user count, and a preview of the compose-window integration.

steps.heading: Install it and grant Gmail permissions
steps.body: Click Add to Chrome and confirm the permissions prompt. Once installed, refresh any Gmail tabs that were already open; extensions granted permission while a tab is open don't always activate until that tab reloads. Pinning the extension to your toolbar makes it easier to reach its settings or turn it off later.

steps.heading: Use it inside a real compose window
steps.body: Open Gmail, click Compose, and the extension's own icons should appear inside the compose toolbar alongside Gmail's formatting and send controls, not in a separate window. Use one of those icons to have it start a message from a short instruction, or continue writing from a line or two you've already typed. The generation happens in the same body field you'd type in, which is the whole point: no switching to a separate ChatGPT tab and pasting a response back.

image.caption: A Gmail compose window with an AI-drafted opening line already in the body — generated in place, without switching to a separate ChatGPT tab.

steps.heading: Read the whole draft before sending
steps.body: Let the tool expand a short prompt into a full message, then read it top to bottom before it goes anywhere. AI-drafted email commonly leaves placeholder brackets like [Product/Service] or [Prospect's Name] that need replacing with real details, and skimming instead of reading the finished draft is the easiest way to miss one. Treat this review as a required step, not an optional one, for anything going to a customer or prospect.

image.caption: A fully drafted follow-up email in Gmail, generated by the extension — note the placeholder text still in the body, which needs to be filled in before sending.

steps.heading: Use the readability and spam-score checks, if the extension includes them
steps.body: Many of these extensions also surface a readability score and a spam-likelihood score for whatever you've written. Running that check before sending a batch of similar emails, like a follow-up sequence, can catch phrasing that would otherwise land in a promotions tab or spam folder. Not every extension includes this; check the listing description before assuming it's there.

troubleshooting.problem: The extension's icons don't show up in Gmail after installing
troubleshooting.cause: It was granted permission while Gmail was already open in a tab, and extensions installed that way don't always activate until the tab reloads.
troubleshooting.fix: Refresh any open Gmail tabs, or restart the browser if a single refresh doesn't pick it up.

troubleshooting.problem: A drafted email still has bracket placeholders like [Prospect's Name] right before you send it
troubleshooting.cause: The draft fills in generic placeholders it expects you to replace, and it doesn't flag them for you on its own.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the entire draft before sending, every time, not just the opening line the tool generated.

troubleshooting.problem: Unsure whether a specific extension is safe to grant inbox access to
troubleshooting.cause: Any extension that inserts tools into Gmail needs broad permission to read and modify the page, which a low-quality or malicious one could misuse.
troubleshooting.fix: Favor an add-on listed on Google Workspace Marketplace, which reviews listings before publishing, and check the developer name, install count, and reviews before granting access.

faq.question: Does ChatGPT connect to Gmail now?
faq.answer: Yes, through OpenAI's own connector in ChatGPT's settings, on paid plans. That version works from the ChatGPT side of things, though; it doesn't add drafting tools inside Gmail's compose window the way a browser extension does.

faq.question: Is it safe to install a Gmail-ChatGPT extension?
faq.answer: Check the developer, rating, and install count before adding one, since any extension working inside Gmail needs permission to read and modify the page. A listing on Google Workspace Marketplace has been through Google's own review, which is one signal worth weighing.

faq.question: What can I automate once it's connected?
faq.answer: Common uses include drafting or rewriting email bodies, generating subject line variations, and checking readability or spam scores, all from inside the normal Gmail compose window.

faq.question: Do I need to edit AI-drafted emails before sending them?
faq.answer: Yes, always. AI drafts often include placeholder text like [Prospect's Name] that needs replacing, and the default tone tends to be generic instead of matched to how you'd normally write to that person.

faq.question: Does any of this cost money?
faq.answer: Extensions usually have a free tier with limits and a paid tier for unlimited use. OpenAI's own chat-side Gmail connector requires a paid ChatGPT plan and isn't available on the free tier.

faq.question: How long does setup take?
faq.answer: Installing an extension and granting Gmail permissions takes a couple of minutes. After that, its tools are available in every new compose window.

verifiedNote: Extension screens and click path come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025. Re-checked in September 2026 against OpenAI's help center and a live Google Workspace Marketplace listing: OpenAI has since shipped its own Gmail connector inside ChatGPT, which this guide previously didn't mention at all and which the intro and FAQ now correct for. The compose-window extension approach in the steps is still a distinct, valid path for anyone who wants suggestions inside Gmail itself instead of in a separate chat.
